teams.heading: Mark Nawaqanitawase's Fiji switch remains unresolved as Sewabu says FRU is watching
teams.body: Mark Nawaqanitawase has not yet confirmed his international allegiance. His agent has said the winger is weighing a possible switch of allegiance, and he is eligible for Fiji, Italy and Australia after serving the three-year stand-down. FRU chief executive Koli Sewabu said: "We are aware of the potential switch Mark could make at the next World Cup and follow this with interest." Wallabies coach Les Kiss says he will wait until the end of the year to see where the winger sits.

lead.why: Returning storyline: the re-check shows no resolution, so the open Nawaqanitawase question still leads.

teams.heading: Manny Feyi-Waboso on track for Australia Test despite Exeter hamstring tweak
teams.body: England's game-breaking wing Manny Feyi-Waboso should be fit for the Nations Championship Test against Australia despite tweaking a hamstring for Exeter against Newcastle. Initial scans showed no major damage, and Exeter's director of rugby Rob Baxter said "there's nothing I'm hearing from our physios saying there should be a long-term issue". Feyi-Waboso misses Exeter's Champions Cup opener at Toulouse, but early indications are said to be positive for a player with nine England tries since his 2024 Six Nations debut.

lead.why: A men's England injury update ahead of the Australia Test is a national-side story, and it is more useful to a fan than the women's result or the Springboks eligibility item.

teams.heading: French prosecutors open probe into Lions lock Hyron Andrews' death
teams.body: French authorities have opened an investigation into the death of Lions lock Hyron Andrews, 31, who was found unresponsive in a locked shower cubicle at the team hotel on the Île de Ré on Friday morning. La Rochelle public prosecutor Arnaud Laraize confirmed to AFP that the case is with the gendarmerie, which is treating it as a suspected accident pending an autopsy, and that there are no signs of violence on his body. The Lions confirmed they would play La Rochelle in Andrews' honour.

lead.why: The only genuinely new item in the shortlist, and it is an investigation on French soil that the French authorities are running.

teams.heading: Ciaran Frawley scores two tries as Connacht beat Saracens with Farrell watching
teams.body: Connacht's 45-36 win over Saracens in the Champions Cup put Ciaran Frawley's form squarely in front of Andy Farrell, who watched from the stands. Frawley led from fly-half and scored two tries, and with Jack Crowley currently sidelined, Planet Rugby expects both Connacht stars to be in Ireland's 23 for November.

teams.heading: Italy still winless after three Nations Championship matches, conceding 131 points
teams.body: Italy go into Round 4 without a win in three matches, sitting 11 of 12 with three defeats, 37 points scored and 131 conceded, a difference of -94. The most recent result was a 10-57 loss to Australia in Round 3. The next opponent is South Africa, who beat Italy 32-14 at home in November 2025 in an international friendly, a single meeting rather than a head-to-head record.

teams.heading: Scotland skipper Sione Tuipulotu's brother finally makes Glasgow Warriors debut
teams.body: Scotland skipper Sione Tuipulotu's childhood dream has been fulfilled, with his brother finally making a Glasgow Warriors debut, according to the Scotsman's report. The coverage ties the milestone to Glasgow's Champions Cup meeting with Sale Sharks, a club fixture rather than a Scotland one, and the report frames the debut as the end of a long wait. Scotland's next fixture is against New Zealand in Round 4.

lead.why: It is the freshest men's item pairing Scotland's captain with a national-side hook, and it avoids re-running the women's story already reported.

teams.heading: Argentina's four-nation 2035 World Cup bid lodged as Spain also bids
teams.body: Argentina are one of four South American nations to submit a joint bid for the 2035 Rugby World Cup, alongside Uruguay, Chile and Brazil, a submission reported in early October. There is no coverage of a host announcement in today's press. The bid must also contend with what Planet Rugby describes as World Rugby's desire for a European return, and Spain has also bid, with a Nou Camp final featuring in its pitch.

teams.heading: All Blacks exploit Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i in Wallabies' 43-21 Accor Stadium defeat
teams.body: Joseph-Aukuso Sua'ali'i's Accor Stadium afternoon is the individual storyline in Planet Rugby's ratings of the 43-21 defeat by New Zealand. The former league man set up an early Wallabies breakaway with a good offload, but then looked lost in defence, was often caught out of position and missed five tackles. The All Blacks exploited him on multiple occasions. Max Jorgensen and Tom Wright drew positive marks for attacking play, with Wright rewarded with a try in the 53rd minute.

lead.why: A new men's XV item naming a Wallabies player, and it avoids the Kiss, rankings and sevens stories already covered.

teams.heading: Japan average 28.1 points scored and 28 conceded in last 11 games
teams.body: Across their last 11 games, Japan have scored 309 points and conceded 308, averages of 28.1 and 28 a game. Their biggest win in that window was 63-14 at home to USA in September, in the Pacific Nations Cup knockout stage. Their last result was a 15-42 defeat to France in Round 3. They are next due to play Wales in Round 4.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie to discuss TMO questions at World Rugby meeting in London
teams.body: Dave Rennie expects the TMO to be a big topic at the World Rugby Shape of the Game meeting in London, after the 43-21 win over the Wallabies. Rennie believes officials correctly ruled that Cam Roigard did not deliberately kick the ball in the tackle that denied Declan Meredith a try, but he asked what happens if it becomes a penalty try. "There are lots of questions to be asked around that."

lead.why: A coach's reaction on a men's national-side officiating question, angled at the All Blacks' stake in the TMO debate, and not already covered in this tab's editions.

teams.heading: Springboks stay No. 1 as All Blacks cut gap to 0.82 points
teams.body: South Africa remain at the top of the World Rugby rankings, but New Zealand have closed in after their 43-21 win over Australia in Sydney. The All Blacks gained 0.46 rating points from that result to move to 92.27, leaving the Springboks on 93.09, a margin of just 0.82. Australia dropped to seventh, while Scotland rose to sixth, in the table as of 17 October.

lead.why: It is the only fresh item on the men's national side in the shortlist, and it concerns South Africa's place at the top of the rankings.
